items.summary: 10 月，我们推荐这 20 位独立开发者，和他们的 100 款产品 DDPM Gen AI DL 极客公园 2026-10-29 20:00 分享 以下文章来源于mp.weixin.qq.com 中科大研一学生 BaiFu 做了一款 Apple Watch 录音应用 Auday，上线一个月左右，冲上了日本和美国 iOS 付费榜的第一名。 还在读高中的唐嘉豪，不想跟着视频做饭时一遍遍拖进度条，就自己做了「口袋厨神」。视频解析、模型调用、服务器存储，整条链路都是他一个人搭的。现在，这款 App 已经上架 App Store。 刘世宇洋是一位科技产业研究员，每周都要做 PPT。因为找不到趁手的图片渐变工具，他自己写了一个网页工具 ImageFader。没花钱推广，靠搜索引擎拿到了第一批自然用户。 过去一段时间，Founder Park 通过产品市集、meetup 活动和社区观察，陆续认识了不少这样的独立开发者。 最直观的感受就是，这个时候的创业和做产品，确实不一样了。有了 coding agent 之后，越来越多的非传统画像的个人开发者开始出现。放在几年前，这些产品多半还得靠一个小团队来做。现在，一个人就能从头到尾做完，而且做得有模有样。不少项目已经正式上架、开始收费，有的在 GitHub 上攒了几万 Star，有的直接冲上了应用榜单。 我们整理了最近遇到的 20 位独立开发者和他们的作品，想看看他们都在做什么产品，是怎么做产品的。 如果你也有自己的项目，欢迎填写下方的产品市集表单，推荐给我们。 ⬆️ 关注 Founder Park，最及时最干货的创业分享 Founder Park 正在 持续寻找值得被看见的 AI 团队与项目。 我们将通过「AI 产品市集」、内容报道、社群分发等方式，帮你触达早期用户、获得真实反馈，以及建立关键连接。 如果你正在做 AI 相关的事，欢迎和我们聊聊。 01 先解决自己日常生活里的痛点 很多产品的起点，小到不太像一个「创业想法」。做饭时手上沾着油，不想再拖进度条。久坐出了毛病，得逼自己多走几步。打开 B 站本来只想查个东西，一抬头半小时没了。偏偏是这些小麻烦，一个人反而更容易从头到尾做完。 BaiFu：中科大研一学生，把 Apple Watch 变成全天录音机 项目：https://auday.ai/ BaiFu 本科毕业于北邮，正在中科大读
items.content: 10 月，我们推荐这 20 位独立开发者，和他们的 100 款产品 DDPM Gen AI DL 极客公园 2026-10-29 20:00 分享 以下文章来源于mp.weixin.qq.com 中科大研一学生 BaiFu 做了一款 Apple Watch 录音应用 Auday，上线一个月左右，冲上了日本和美国 iOS 付费榜的第一名。 还在读高中的唐嘉豪，不想跟着视频做饭时一遍遍拖进度条，就自己做了「口袋厨神」。视频解析、模型调用、服务器存储，整条链路都是他一个人搭的。现在，这款 App 已经上架 App Store。 刘世宇洋是一位科技产业研究员，每周都要做 PPT。因为找不到趁手的图片渐变工具，他自己写了一个网页工具 ImageFader。没花钱推广，靠搜索引擎拿到了第一批自然用户。 过去一段时间，Founder Park 通过产品市集、meetup 活动和社区观察，陆续认识了不少这样的独立开发者。 最直观的感受就是，这个时候的创业和做产品，确实不一样了。有了 coding agent 之后，越来越多的非传统画像的个人开发者开始出现。放在几年前，这些产品多半还得靠一个小团队来做。现在，一个人就能从头到尾做完，而且做得有模有样。不少项目已经正式上架、开始收费，有的在 GitHub 上攒了几万 Star，有的直接冲上了应用榜单。 我们整理了最近遇到的 20 位独立开发者和他们的作品，想看看他们都在做什么产品，是怎么做产品的。 如果你也有自己的项目，欢迎填写下方的产品市集表单，推荐给我们。 ⬆️ 关注 Founder Park，最及时最干货的创业分享 Founder Park 正在 持续寻找值得被看见的 AI 团队与项目。 我们将通过「AI 产品市集」、内容报道、社群分发等方式，帮你触达早期用户、获得真实反馈，以及建立关键连接。 如果你正在做 AI 相关的事，欢迎和我们聊聊。 01 先解决自己日常生活里的痛点 很多产品的起点，小到不太像一个「创业想法」。做饭时手上沾着油，不想再拖进度条。久坐出了毛病，得逼自己多走几步。打开 B 站本来只想查个东西，一抬头半小时没了。偏偏是这些小麻烦，一个人反而更容易从头到尾做完。 BaiFu：中科大研一学生，把 Apple Watch 变成全天录音机 项目：https://auday.ai/ BaiFu 本科毕业于北邮，正在中科大读研一。在开源圈，他其实已经小有名气。他从零写的多 Agent 舆情分析系统 BettaFish 有 4 万多 Star，盛大创始人陈天桥看到后找来合作。他又在盛大支持下用十天做出群体智能预测引擎 MiroFish，拿下了 8 万多 Star。 但做 Auday 时，他特意新开了一个 X 账号从头冷启动。他想看看，不靠之前的名气，产品自己能不能跑出来。 Auday 把 Apple Watch 变成了一台全天候的录音机。和常见的录音摘要工具不太一样，它会把对话和手表记下的心率、压力、位置放进同一条时间轴。回头翻的时候，不光能找到那句原话，还能想起那句话是在什么情况下说的。在 BaiFu 看来，录音不只是用来提取信息，声音本身也是一种记忆。 决定自己动手做 Auday 之前，BaiFu 买过至少五款 AI 录音设备。录音卡、超薄录音器都用过，没有一个让他满意。后来他想明白了，最适合全天录音的硬件，其实就是已经戴在很多人手腕上的 Apple Watch。大家本来就习惯了戴着它、每天充电，根本不需要再多带一个硬件。 Auday 价格 9.99 美元，一次买断。上线一个月左右，先后登上了日本、美国等地 iOS 付费榜的第一名。 唐嘉豪：还在读高中，已经一个人做过四款产品 产品：https://pocketchef.zhiheschool.com/ 唐嘉豪目前还在读高中，但「口袋厨神」并不是他做的第一个完整产品。在这之前，他还做过一款 Steam 游戏、一个健康类小程序，给学校写过考勤系统。 平时跟着小红书、B 站做饭总要拖进度条，他就自己做了口袋厨神。贴入视频链接，它会整理出用料和步骤，再按时间戳截下关键步骤的画面。拍张冰箱里的食材照片，或者随口说个想吃的东西，它也能给你生成菜谱。 视频下载和存储、接通义千问 VL 抽帧，再到架中转服务器调 Gemini，整套链路全是唐嘉豪一个人搭的。 去年底，口袋厨神还只是一个小程序，有 700 多用户，单日新增最多 200 多人，每天成本三四十块。当时订阅还没上线，他算了笔账，觉得量一下起来自己扛不住，宁可先不推流量。现在口袋厨神已经上架 iOS，App Store 评分 4.9，也有了按月、季、年付费的会员。 丁川：设计师做了一只 AI 宠物，你走多少步，它就旅行多远 产品：https://www.pawstep.fun/ 丁川是设计师。因为久坐查出轻度静脉曲张，医生让他多走路。试了一圈计步软件后，有两年 Vibe Coding 经验的他决定换个思路，把冷冰冰的步数进度条换成角色和故事。 他做的「爪步」玩法有点像《旅行青蛙》。选一座城市，派一只 AI 宠物过去，你每天走的步数，就是它的路费。它会一路给你写信、发动态，讲它在京都、巴厘岛、成都碰到了什么。宠物们性格各不相同，狐獴嘴硬心软，浣熊毒舌但靠谱，哪天走得少了还会调侃你两句。 整个产品很少提健康指标，进度条换成了角色和故事。丁川也在琢磨，把宠物带到 AI 眼镜这类硬件上，或者跟潮玩做联名。 常亮：做过推荐算法的人，开始帮用户逃离推荐流 项目：https://www.aibrotherwatch.com/zh-CN/ 常亮在字节做过一年多广告推荐算法，之后在文远知行做了四年研发。去年 8 月出来全职做产品，他选的方向，刚好跟老本行反着来。 AI Brother 是一个 Chrome 插件。装上以后，B 站、知乎、小红书的首页只剩下一个搜索框。你先跟它说清楚现在要干什么，AI 会在后台判断你正在看的东西和这件事有没有关系。一旦发现你看偏了，屏幕上就会跳出一只小猫提醒「小猫咪在看着你」。 Baye：独立开发八年，一直在维护一款短信拦截 App 产品：https://baye.tech/ Baye 做独立开发已经八年多了，不融资、不卖广告，卖 App。 他做的「熊猫吃短信」，拦截垃圾短信，不联网，不上传短信，识别全在手机本地完成。最初的样本库是他自己花两周手工标注的，后来靠用户举报，样本攒到了上百万条。一代卖 3 块钱买断，上过很多次 App Store 推荐，也冲到过付费榜第一。到了二代，模型架构换了，还能把短信细分成财务、订单、运营商等类别，而且至今几乎每周都在更新。 Baye 还有一款路子完全相反的产品，OpenCat。OpenAI 开放 API 的第二天，他就做出了这款 ChatGPT「套壳」应用，正好赶上时间窗口，后来攒下了几十万用 户。他自己说，这是他「做的最没技术含量的产品」。 Gatheon：工作里的每个痛点，都给自己定制了一款软件 产品：https://gatheon.com/ 这是个略显神秘的开发者，自称是工具控，每年在效率工具上的花费超过 2 万元。 目前已上线接近 10 款产品，其中最打动我的是截图日历和声忆，前者解决了微信里跟创业者聊天约线下会议的痛点；后者是一个完成度很高的语音输入法，支持本地模型和调用 api，支持语音的分析和梳理，支持一键发送想法到各类笔记软件里，比如我最常用的 flomo。 功能都不一定是独创的，但都是基于个人的工作场景里的实际需求和痛点，进行的个人定制化的开发。 感谢这个 Vibe Coding 时代，每个人的需求都有被看到和被解决的机会。 02 工作流里能提效的一点点， 也是机会 坐到办公桌前，每个人每天都会碰到几个不太顺手的时刻。为了翻译一句话来回切窗口、给 PPT 里的图片修个渐变边、电脑用久了越来越卡。这些事单拎出来都不大，也很少有大公司专门去做。可对天天碰到它的人来说，自己动手做一个，可能反而是最快的办法。 图拉鼎：做了十几年 Mac 应用，给自己定下「三个月交出第一版」 产品：https://poptranslate.app/ 图拉鼎在 Apple 生态里做了十几年软件。大学时写过 Ubuntu Tweak，后来转做 macOS 应用，Manico、One Switch 和 PasteNow 这些小工具，很多 Mac 老用户都装过。 他曾花一年多时间做了个网络收藏工具 MarkMark。战线拉得太长，越做越累。这次的新产品 PopTranslate，从设计到发布，用了三个月。他的经验是，一个人做产品，第一版最好在三个月内拿出来，别长期陷在技术方案里。 PopTranslate 把查词和改写的动作压到了最短。在 Mac 任意应用里选中文本，鼠标旁直接弹出工具栏，当场完成翻译、解释和改写。翻译功能最早是为了让妻子看外文网页更方便。英文改写则来自他自己回海外用户邮件的习惯，先用英文把大意写出来，再让 AI 顺一顺。 刘世宇洋：每周都做 PPT 的研究员，做了一个图片渐变工具 项目：https://imagefader.com 刘世宇洋是科技产业研究员，对自己的介绍是：「每周都在做 PPT。」 写报告做 PPT 时，他经常需要让图片边缘自然淡出去。市面上的工具要么收费，要么导出的是白色遮罩「假透明」，放到深色背景上就会露出一圈白边。他干脆自己做了网页工具 ImageFader，支持线性、径向和扇形渐变，也能圈出一块区域单独做局部羽化，导出真正的半透明通道。整个网站很轻，处理全在浏览器里完成，不用注册，也不上传服务器。 刘世宇洋没花钱推广，只是给每种渐变模式都单独做了 SEO 落地页，上线后很快通过细分搜索词，拿到了第一批用户。工具目前免费，他最近在思考，下一步是把图片处理能力做成 MCP 给 Agent 调用，还是干脆自己做一个 Agent 产品。 林志煌：连发一排新工具，每个都给 Agent 留好入口 项目：https://www.oiloil.org/ 林志煌最近上线的东西有点多。打开 oiloil.org，能看到一整排产品：设计 Skill Oil UI、录屏剪辑工具 Oil Studio、Mac 文件搜索 Oil Find、Git 可视化工具 Oil Git，还有之前做的 VibeHub。 他之前在 API7.ai 做前端兼产品经理。现在自己做产品，不管是做设计、剪视频还是看代码，他都会专门给 Agent 留一个入口。 其中，Oil UI 是一个给 Claude Code、Codex 这类 Agent 用的 UI 设计 Skill，想解决 AI 做出来的界面总是长得差不多的问题。 它会先找同类产品里风格鲜明的参考，把「高级」「干净」落成具体的字体、留白和用色，一次拿出几套不同方向给你挑，选定后再对照真实截图一轮轮修改。开源版在 GitHub 上已有 2400 多 Star，另外还有一个 9.99 美元买断的 Pro 版。 Sai：自学编程的数字游民，做了个带 Agent 的无限画布 项目：https://polox.ai Sai 是自学编程的数字游民，有了 Vibe Coding 之后，他更愿意把自己叫作 AI PM。他对产品有个执念，所有功能都从 Agent 这一个入口进去，用户能少点一下，就少点一下。 他做的 PoloX AI 是一张带 Agent 的无限画布。你在对话里讲需求，Agent 去调用生图、改图、生视频的能力，结果直接铺在画布上，选中哪张，就接着聊哪张。不用在几个平台之间来回导文件，也不用自己写长 prompt、调参数。生成视频前，Agent 还会弹出一张卡片，把能用的模型和大概的成本列出来给你选。 PoloX AI 已经做得相当完整，开源版基于 DeepSeek Harness 搭建，在 Product Hunt、V2EX、观猹上都有人转发。 tw93：一个自用一年的清理脚本，在泳池边变成了 7 万 Star 的项目 项目：https://github.com/tw93/Mole tw93 是前端工程师，有正职，也有家要顾。他手里的出圈项目不少，一条命令把网页打包成桌面 App 的 Pake 拿下了 6 万多 Star，原生 Markdown 编辑器妙言，还有从近一年 Claude 对话里提炼出的工程技能库 Waza，最初都是他做给自己用的。 今年的新爆款 Mole 也是这么来的。他的 Mac 上一直跑着一个自己写的清理脚本，用了快一年，越写越长，攒到将近一千行。之前去三亚度假时，他在泳池边把它重写成了正式的命令行工具 Mole，把清缓存、清日志和删残留收进几条命令里。现在它在 GitHub 上有 7.3 万多 Star，七成以上的用户来自海外。 低空飞行：开源自研桌面框架后，做了款人和 Agent 都能用的视频下载工具 项目：https://downbit.app/zh 低空飞行在开源圈是老面孔了，tsup、poi 和 docute 这些前端工具，还有桌面 AI 客户端 ChatWise 都出自他手。 最近这一个月，他一直在围绕自己写的 Go 桌面框架 mygo 高密度出活。9 月底框架刚开源，他在两周里接连做出 2048、终端 gorex、diff 查看器 godiff 和菜单栏统计工具 uma。紧接着，又上线了新产品 Downbit，一个下载网页音视频的跨平台原生应用。 市面上很多视频下载工具，底层用的都是 Python、yt-dlp 和 FFmpeg。Downbit 是他用 Go 从头写成，不依赖这些外部组件，连音视频合并也是内置的 Go 封装器自己完成。除了支持 B 站、小红书、抖音和 YouTube 等常见平台，碰到没适配的网页，用内置的浏览器打开、播放一下，就能直接把视频和音频抓下来。 Agent 用起来也很方便。Downbit 既是桌面软件，也是命令行。不带参数时打开界面，带上参数就直接执行命令。所有命令都能输出 JSON，脚本和 Agent 都能直接调用。 easychen：独立开发 20 年，这次把旧手机做成了看板 项目：https://sudo.ft07.com/ easychen 做独立开发已经 20 年了。Server 酱、Check 酱和 CookieCloud 都是他的作品，他写的开源小书《程序员如何优雅地挣零花钱》《一人企业方法论》，在 GitHub 上合计拿到了超过 3.5 万 Star。 今年他做的 SudoBoard，可以把家里吃灰的旧手机、平板或电视变成自动刷新的数据看板。拿来做小店的门店信息屏、团队的 KPI 大屏或者客服工作台都可以，不用再专门去买一块大屏硬件。 数据能接 API、数据库或 Excel。配置看板可以一句话交给 AI 生成页面，日常抓数据和刷新页面，还是让普通程序去跑。不用每次调用模型，也就不会一直烧 Token。 03 围绕 Agent， 长出了一批「伺候 Agent」的工具 用 Codex、Claude Code 的人越来越多，不少人还是好几个一起开。随之冒出来的是一堆新麻烦：怎么让 Agent 读懂需要登录的网页？怎么在不同工具之间切模型、省 Token？后台同时跑着几个任务时，怎么知道哪个跑完了？ Agent 越能干活，周边的活儿就越多。给 Agent 修路、做总控台、建工作群，正在长成一批独立产品。 卡比卡比：拿到 3 万 Star 后推倒重来，让 Agent 直接用上你登录好的 Chrome 项目：https://github.com/jackwener/BrowserMCP 卡比卡比是 Apache Arrow、DataFusion 和 Doris 三个项目的 PMC 成员，之前在字节和 SelectDB 做数据库。 今年 3 月，他做的 OpenCLI 在 GitHub 上拿到了 3 万多 Star，能借用本地 Chrome 已登录的账号，把几十个网站变成可直接调用的命令。到了 9 月，他把 OpenCLI 推倒重来，做成了 opencli-mcp（现在叫 BrowserMCP）。 Agent 不用再记一堆命令，通过 MCP 直接操作已经登录的 Chrome，搜索、读网页和填表单都可以。碰到没适配过的页面，Agent 也能自己写代码去操作。用他自己的话说：「浏览器之于人，OpenCLI 之于 Agent。」 Zen：让 Agent 直接「读」你浏览器里打开的网页 项目：https://dokobot.ai/ 让 Agent 读网页，经常要过三道坎：要登录，要等页面加载完，还有反爬。就算抓下来了，一大坨 HTML 塞进上下文，Token 也花得飞快。 Zen 全职做了快一年的 Dokobot，只专心做「读」这一件事。它通过命令行连上本地 Chrome，直接读取已经登录、加载好的页面，再整理成 Markdown 交给 Agent。据说，这样能省下 80% 到 99% 的 Token。它按页面的视觉布局来理解内容，不靠解析网页代码，网站改版了也没那么容易失效。 本地模式免费、不限量，不用注册，数据也不会离开你的电脑。Zen 接下来想往便宜又好用的 Deep Research 方向走。 yetone：一个菜单栏，管理所有 Agent 的模型、订阅和 Token 项目：https://usemagpie.ai/ yetone 之前在豆瓣、第四范式与旷视工作过，也在 BentoML 做过资深 MLOps 工程师。9 月 23 日，他发布了菜单栏工具 Magpie。一周就有 3000 多 Star，现在已经超过 2.4 万，几乎每天都在连着发版。 Magpie 解决的是同时用几个 Agent 改配置太麻烦的问题。哪个 Agent 正在用哪个模型，在菜单栏里点一下就能换，背后的本地网关会把几家不同的 API 协议实时互译。 Magpie 还能共享订阅。你在某个 Agent 里登录过 Claude Pro 或者 ChatGPT Plus，这份订阅就能拿给其他 Agent 一起用。它还会在本地回放真实的调用记录，算出什么时候压缩上下文最省 Token。 yetone 有句话说得很直接，「Agent 时代，模型之间差距没有想象中大，Harness 的差距才是真的，一切 Infra 都值得为 Agent 重新写一遍。」 Jason Young：改配置太麻烦，催生了一个近 15 万 Star 的项目 项目：https://www.ccswitch.io/ 说到 Magpie，国内社区最常拿来跟它比的，是 CC Switch。去年 8 月上线以来，这个基于 Tauri 2 和 Rust 的跨平台桌面工具，已经在 GitHub 上攒下了近 15 万颗 Star 和 9800 多次 Fork。 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI、OpenCode 各有一套 API Key、接口地址和模型配置，要在不同供应商、中转服务之间来回切换，只能手动改文件。CC Switch 把这些都放进了一个界面里，一键就能切换，MCP、Prompts、Skills 也能统一管理，在各家花了多少钱也看得清楚。 JoyWong：给 Agent 当监工，还卖起了角色和声音 项目：https://agentbell.dev/ 同时开着几个窗口让 Agent 干活时，人总得时不时切回去看一眼进度。JoyWong 做的 AgentBell 是一个 macOS 菜单栏应用，专门替你盯着这几个工具里 Agent 的状态。 任务跑完了、出错了、在等你确认，或者半天没动静，它都会在菜单栏提醒你，桌面上的小角色也会跳出来喊你，还能用语音播报出来。Agent 闲下来的时候，它就给你播几条 AI 和科技新闻。 它收费的地方也挺有意思，卖的是角色和声音，比如温柔治愈的 Hiyori、暴躁码农疯狂兔子、黑客风的码猫。一个效率工具，顺手做起了陪伴。 idoubi：裸辞两年上线 20 多款产品，这次给 Agent 做了个「微信」 项目：https://github.com/thinkany-ai/douchat idoubi 在腾讯做过五年后台开发。2023 年裸辞后，他在两年多里一口气上线了 20 多款产品，包括 AI 搜索 ThinkAny、月访问量峰值 270 万的 MCP 应用市场 MCP.so，以及预售四小时破万美元的 SaaS 模板 ShipAny，还写了一本《这就是 MCP》。 今年 10 月，他开源了新作品 douchat，定位是「Agent 版微信」。它会自动找出你电脑上的 Codex、Claude Code 等本地 Agent，把它们变成可以拉进群的「联系人」。你、你的同事，还有你们各自的 Agent，可以待在同一个群里讨论、派活，共享同一份上下文。 同期，他还开源了连接器平台 Connany，五分钟内帮任意 Agent 统一接上 Notion 与 GitHub 等 25 个外部服务。 benn：让人和不同的 Agent 共享同一段对话 项目：https://sumus.im/ benn 也是前腾讯高级工程师。他之前一个人做出了 AI 客户端 Chatbox，在 GitHub 上拿到 4 万多 Star，后来产品被收购。从做出来到卖出去，一个独立产品能走的路，他已经完整走过一遍了。 他的新产品 Sumus 从 9 月开始公测，想解决的问题是，你调好了一个很好用的 Agent，想让朋友、同事也一起用，该怎么办？分享配置或模板是一种办法，但之前聊过的内容、积累下来的上下文，都带不过去。 Sumus 的做法，是把人、云端 Agent 和本地 Agent 都拉进同一段对话。云端 Agent 负责查资料、做规划，本地 Agent 负责写代码、执行。所有人都能在同一个对话流里继续追问、补充上下文。 更多阅读 Manus 内部复盘：一家 Agent 公司，如何先用 Agent 改造自己？ 对话K2 Lab王铭：Muse帮人省钱，Moras帮人赚钱，这才是垂直赛道Personal AI的刚需 聊Agent商业化、做AI产品、链接全球资源，近期这些活动别错过 items.raw_text: 10 月，我们推荐这 20 位独立开发者，和他们的 100 款产品 DDPM Gen AI DL 极客公园 2026-10-29 20:00 分享 以下文章来源于mp.weixin.qq.com 中科大研一学生 BaiFu 做了一款 Apple Watch 录音应用 Auday，上线一个月左右，冲上了日本和美国 iOS 付费榜的第一名。 还在读高中的唐嘉豪，不想跟着视频做饭时一遍遍拖进度条，就自己做了「口袋厨神」。视频解析、模型调用、服务器存储，整条链路都是他一个人搭的。现在，这款 App 已经上架 App Store。 刘世宇洋是一位科技产业研究员，每周都要做 PPT。因为找不到趁手的图片渐变工具，他自己写了一个网页工具 ImageFader。没花钱推广，靠搜索引擎拿到了第一批自然用户。 过去一段时间，Founder Park 通过产品市集、meetup 活动和社区观察，陆续认识了不少这样的独立开发者。 最直观的感受就是，这个时候的创业和做产品，确实不一样了。有了 coding agent 之后，越来越多的非传统画像的个人开发者开始出现。放在几年前，这些产品多半还得靠一个小团队来做。现在，一个人就能从头到尾做完，而且做得有模有样。不少项目已经正式上架、开始收费，有的在 GitHub 上攒了几万 Star，有的直接冲上了应用榜单。 我们整理了最近遇到的 20 位独立开发者和他们的作品，想看看他们都在做什么产品，是怎么做产品的。 如果你也有自己的项目，欢迎填写下方的产品市集表单，推荐给我们。 ⬆️ 关注 Founder Park，最及时最干货的创业分享 Founder Park 正在 持续寻找值得被看见的 AI 团队与项目。 我们将通过「AI 产品市集」、内容报道、社群分发等方式，帮你触达早期用户、获得真实反馈，以及建立关键连接。 如果你正在做 AI 相关的事，欢迎和我们聊聊。 01 先解决自己日常生活里的痛点 很多产品的起点，小到不太像一个「创业想法」。做饭时手上沾着油，不想再拖进度条。久坐出了毛病，得逼自己多走几步。打开 B 站本来只想查个东西，一抬头半小时没了。偏偏是这些小麻烦，一个人反而更容易从头到尾做完。 BaiFu：中科大研一学生，把 Apple Watch 变成全天录音机 项目：https://auday.ai/ BaiFu 本科毕业于北邮，正在中科大读研一。在开源圈，他其实已经小有名气。他从零写的多 Agent 舆情分析系统 BettaFish 有 4 万多 Star，盛大创始人陈天桥看到后找来合作。他又在盛大支持下用十天做出群体智能预测引擎 MiroFish，拿下了 8 万多 Star。 但做 Auday 时，他特意新开了一个 X 账号从头冷启动。他想看看，不靠之前的名气，产品自己能不能跑出来。 Auday 把 Apple Watch 变成了一台全天候的录音机。和常见的录音摘要工具不太一样，它会把对话和手表记下的心率、压力、位置放进同一条时间轴。回头翻的时候，不光能找到那句原话，还能想起那句话是在什么情况下说的。在 BaiFu 看来，录音不只是用来提取信息，声音本身也是一种记忆。 决定自己动手做 Auday 之前，BaiFu 买过至少五款 AI 录音设备。录音卡、超薄录音器都用过，没有一个让他满意。后来他想明白了，最适合全天录音的硬件，其实就是已经戴在很多人手腕上的 Apple Watch。大家本来就习惯了戴着它、每天充电，根本不需要再多带一个硬件。 Auday 价格 9.99 美元，一次买断。上线一个月左右，先后登上了日本、美国等地 iOS 付费榜的第一名。 唐嘉豪：还在读高中，已经一个人做过四款产品 产品：https://pocketchef.zhiheschool.com/ 唐嘉豪目前还在读高中，但「口袋厨神」并不是他做的第一个完整产品。在这之前，他还做过一款 Steam 游戏、一个健康类小程序，给学校写过考勤系统。 平时跟着小红书、B 站做饭总要拖进度条，他就自己做了口袋厨神。贴入视频链接，它会整理出用料和步骤，再按时间戳截下关键步骤的画面。拍张冰箱里的食材照片，或者随口说个想吃的东西，它也能给你生成菜谱。 视频下载和存储、接通义千问 VL 抽帧，再到架中转服务器调 Gemini，整套链路全是唐嘉豪一个人搭的。 去年底，口袋厨神还只是一个小程序，有 700 多用户，单日新增最多 200 多人，每天成本三四十块。当时订阅还没上线，他算了笔账，觉得量一下起来自己扛不住，宁可先不推流量。现在口袋厨神已经上架 iOS，App Store 评分 4.9，也有了按月、季、年付费的会员。 丁川：设计师做了一只 AI 宠物，你走多少步，它就旅行多远 产品：https://www.pawstep.fun/ 丁川是设计师。因为久坐查出轻度静脉曲张，医生让他多走路。试了一圈计步软件后，有两年 Vibe Coding 经验的他决定换个思路，把冷冰冰的步数进度条换成角色和故事。 他做的「爪步」玩法有点像《旅行青蛙》。选一座城市，派一只 AI 宠物过去，你每天走的步数，就是它的路费。它会一路给你写信、发动态，讲它在京都、巴厘岛、成都碰到了什么。宠物们性格各不相同，狐獴嘴硬心软，浣熊毒舌但靠谱，哪天走得少了还会调侃你两句。 整个产品很少提健康指标，进度条换成了角色和故事。丁川也在琢磨，把宠物带到 AI 眼镜这类硬件上，或者跟潮玩做联名。 常亮：做过推荐算法的人，开始帮用户逃离推荐流 项目：https://www.aibrotherwatch.com/zh-CN/ 常亮在字节做过一年多广告推荐算法，之后在文远知行做了四年研发。去年 8 月出来全职做产品，他选的方向，刚好跟老本行反着来。 AI Brother 是一个 Chrome 插件。装上以后，B 站、知乎、小红书的首页只剩下一个搜索框。你先跟它说清楚现在要干什么，AI 会在后台判断你正在看的东西和这件事有没有关系。一旦发现你看偏了，屏幕上就会跳出一只小猫提醒「小猫咪在看着你」。 Baye：独立开发八年，一直在维护一款短信拦截 App 产品：https://baye.tech/ Baye 做独立开发已经八年多了，不融资、不卖广告，卖 App。 他做的「熊猫吃短信」，拦截垃圾短信，不联网，不上传短信，识别全在手机本地完成。最初的样本库是他自己花两周手工标注的，后来靠用户举报，样本攒到了上百万条。一代卖 3 块钱买断，上过很多次 App Store 推荐，也冲到过付费榜第一。到了二代，模型架构换了，还能把短信细分成财务、订单、运营商等类别，而且至今几乎每周都在更新。 Baye 还有一款路子完全相反的产品，OpenCat。OpenAI 开放 API 的第二天，他就做出了这款 ChatGPT「套壳」应用，正好赶上时间窗口，后来攒下了几十万用 户。他自己说，这是他「做的最没技术含量的产品」。 Gatheon：工作里的每个痛点，都给自己定制了一款软件 产品：https://gatheon.com/ 这是个略显神秘的开发者，自称是工具控，每年在效率工具上的花费超过 2 万元。 目前已上线接近 10 款产品，其中最打动我的是截图日历和声忆，前者解决了微信里跟创业者聊天约线下会议的痛点；后者是一个完成度很高的语音输入法，支持本地模型和调用 api，支持语音的分析和梳理，支持一键发送想法到各类笔记软件里，比如我最常用的 flomo。 功能都不一定是独创的，但都是基于个人的工作场景里的实际需求和痛点，进行的个人定制化的开发。 感谢这个 Vibe Coding 时代，每个人的需求都有被看到和被解决的机会。 02 工作流里能提效的一点点， 也是机会 坐到办公桌前，每个人每天都会碰到几个不太顺手的时刻。为了翻译一句话来回切窗口、给 PPT 里的图片修个渐变边、电脑用久了越来越卡。这些事单拎出来都不大，也很少有大公司专门去做。可对天天碰到它的人来说，自己动手做一个，可能反而是最快的办法。 图拉鼎：做了十几年 Mac 应用，给自己定下「三个月交出第一版」 产品：https://poptranslate.app/ 图拉鼎在 Apple 生态里做了十几年软件。大学时写过 Ubuntu Tweak，后来转做 macOS 应用，Manico、One Switch 和 PasteNow 这些小工具，很多 Mac 老用户都装过。 他曾花一年多时间做了个网络收藏工具 MarkMark。战线拉得太长，越做越累。这次的新产品 PopTranslate，从设计到发布，用了三个月。他的经验是，一个人做产品，第一版最好在三个月内拿出来，别长期陷在技术方案里。 PopTranslate 把查词和改写的动作压到了最短。在 Mac 任意应用里选中文本，鼠标旁直接弹出工具栏，当场完成翻译、解释和改写。翻译功能最早是为了让妻子看外文网页更方便。英文改写则来自他自己回海外用户邮件的习惯，先用英文把大意写出来，再让 AI 顺一顺。 刘世宇洋：每周都做 PPT 的研究员，做了一个图片渐变工具 项目：https://imagefader.com 刘世宇洋是科技产业研究员，对自己的介绍是：「每周都在做 PPT。」 写报告做 PPT 时，他经常需要让图片边缘自然淡出去。市面上的工具要么收费，要么导出的是白色遮罩「假透明」，放到深色背景上就会露出一圈白边。他干脆自己做了网页工具 ImageFader，支持线性、径向和扇形渐变，也能圈出一块区域单独做局部羽化，导出真正的半透明通道。整个网站很轻，处理全在浏览器里完成，不用注册，也不上传服务器。 刘世宇洋没花钱推广，只是给每种渐变模式都单独做了 SEO 落地页，上线后很快通过细分搜索词，拿到了第一批用户。工具目前免费，他最近在思考，下一步是把图片处理能力做成 MCP 给 Agent 调用，还是干脆自己做一个 Agent 产品。 林志煌：连发一排新工具，每个都给 Agent 留好入口 项目：https://www.oiloil.org/ 林志煌最近上线的东西有点多。打开 oiloil.org，能看到一整排产品：设计 Skill Oil UI、录屏剪辑工具 Oil Studio、Mac 文件搜索 Oil Find、Git 可视化工具 Oil Git，还有之前做的 VibeHub。 他之前在 API7.ai 做前端兼产品经理。现在自己做产品，不管是做设计、剪视频还是看代码，他都会专门给 Agent 留一个入口。 其中，Oil UI 是一个给 Claude Code、Codex 这类 Agent 用的 UI 设计 Skill，想解决 AI 做出来的界面总是长得差不多的问题。 它会先找同类产品里风格鲜明的参考，把「高级」「干净」落成具体的字体、留白和用色，一次拿出几套不同方向给你挑，选定后再对照真实截图一轮轮修改。开源版在 GitHub 上已有 2400 多 Star，另外还有一个 9.99 美元买断的 Pro 版。 Sai：自学编程的数字游民，做了个带 Agent 的无限画布 项目：https://polox.ai Sai 是自学编程的数字游民，有了 Vibe Coding 之后，他更愿意把自己叫作 AI PM。他对产品有个执念，所有功能都从 Agent 这一个入口进去，用户能少点一下，就少点一下。 他做的 PoloX AI 是一张带 Agent 的无限画布。你在对话里讲需求，Agent 去调用生图、改图、生视频的能力，结果直接铺在画布上，选中哪张，就接着聊哪张。不用在几个平台之间来回导文件，也不用自己写长 prompt、调参数。生成视频前，Agent 还会弹出一张卡片，把能用的模型和大概的成本列出来给你选。 PoloX AI 已经做得相当完整，开源版基于 DeepSeek Harness 搭建，在 Product Hunt、V2EX、观猹上都有人转发。 tw93：一个自用一年的清理脚本，在泳池边变成了 7 万 Star 的项目 项目：https://github.com/tw93/Mole tw93 是前端工程师，有正职，也有家要顾。他手里的出圈项目不少，一条命令把网页打包成桌面 App 的 Pake 拿下了 6 万多 Star，原生 Markdown 编辑器妙言，还有从近一年 Claude 对话里提炼出的工程技能库 Waza，最初都是他做给自己用的。 今年的新爆款 Mole 也是这么来的。他的 Mac 上一直跑着一个自己写的清理脚本，用了快一年，越写越长，攒到将近一千行。之前去三亚度假时，他在泳池边把它重写成了正式的命令行工具 Mole，把清缓存、清日志和删残留收进几条命令里。现在它在 GitHub 上有 7.3 万多 Star，七成以上的用户来自海外。 低空飞行：开源自研桌面框架后，做了款人和 Agent 都能用的视频下载工具 项目：https://downbit.app/zh 低空飞行在开源圈是老面孔了，tsup、poi 和 docute 这些前端工具，还有桌面 AI 客户端 ChatWise 都出自他手。 最近这一个月，他一直在围绕自己写的 Go 桌面框架 mygo 高密度出活。9 月底框架刚开源，他在两周里接连做出 2048、终端 gorex、diff 查看器 godiff 和菜单栏统计工具 uma。紧接着，又上线了新产品 Downbit，一个下载网页音视频的跨平台原生应用。 市面上很多视频下载工具，底层用的都是 Python、yt-dlp 和 FFmpeg。Downbit 是他用 Go 从头写成，不依赖这些外部组件，连音视频合并也是内置的 Go 封装器自己完成。除了支持 B 站、小红书、抖音和 YouTube 等常见平台，碰到没适配的网页，用内置的浏览器打开、播放一下，就能直接把视频和音频抓下来。 Agent 用起来也很方便。Downbit 既是桌面软件，也是命令行。不带参数时打开界面，带上参数就直接执行命令。所有命令都能输出 JSON，脚本和 Agent 都能直接调用。 easychen：独立开发 20 年，这次把旧手机做成了看板 项目：https://sudo.ft07.com/ easychen 做独立开发已经 20 年了。Server 酱、Check 酱和 CookieCloud 都是他的作品，他写的开源小书《程序员如何优雅地挣零花钱》《一人企业方法论》，在 GitHub 上合计拿到了超过 3.5 万 Star。 今年他做的 SudoBoard，可以把家里吃灰的旧手机、平板或电视变成自动刷新的数据看板。拿来做小店的门店信息屏、团队的 KPI 大屏或者客服工作台都可以，不用再专门去买一块大屏硬件。 数据能接 API、数据库或 Excel。配置看板可以一句话交给 AI 生成页面，日常抓数据和刷新页面，还是让普通程序去跑。不用每次调用模型，也就不会一直烧 Token。 03 围绕 Agent， 长出了一批「伺候 Agent」的工具 用 Codex、Claude Code 的人越来越多，不少人还是好几个一起开。随之冒出来的是一堆新麻烦：怎么让 Agent 读懂需要登录的网页？怎么在不同工具之间切模型、省 Token？后台同时跑着几个任务时，怎么知道哪个跑完了？ Agent 越能干活，周边的活儿就越多。给 Agent 修路、做总控台、建工作群，正在长成一批独立产品。 卡比卡比：拿到 3 万 Star 后推倒重来，让 Agent 直接用上你登录好的 Chrome 项目：https://github.com/jackwener/BrowserMCP 卡比卡比是 Apache Arrow、DataFusion 和 Doris 三个项目的 PMC 成员，之前在字节和 SelectDB 做数据库。 今年 3 月，他做的 OpenCLI 在 GitHub 上拿到了 3 万多 Star，能借用本地 Chrome 已登录的账号，把几十个网站变成可直接调用的命令。到了 9 月，他把 OpenCLI 推倒重来，做成了 opencli-mcp（现在叫 BrowserMCP）。 Agent 不用再记一堆命令，通过 MCP 直接操作已经登录的 Chrome，搜索、读网页和填表单都可以。碰到没适配过的页面，Agent 也能自己写代码去操作。用他自己的话说：「浏览器之于人，OpenCLI 之于 Agent。」 Zen：让 Agent 直接「读」你浏览器里打开的网页 项目：https://dokobot.ai/ 让 Agent 读网页，经常要过三道坎：要登录，要等页面加载完，还有反爬。就算抓下来了，一大坨 HTML 塞进上下文，Token 也花得飞快。 Zen 全职做了快一年的 Dokobot，只专心做「读」这一件事。它通过命令行连上本地 Chrome，直接读取已经登录、加载好的页面，再整理成 Markdown 交给 Agent。据说，这样能省下 80% 到 99% 的 Token。它按页面的视觉布局来理解内容，不靠解析网页代码，网站改版了也没那么容易失效。 本地模式免费、不限量，不用注册，数据也不会离开你的电脑。Zen 接下来想往便宜又好用的 Deep Research 方向走。 yetone：一个菜单栏，管理所有 Agent 的模型、订阅和 Token 项目：https://usemagpie.ai/ yetone 之前在豆瓣、第四范式与旷视工作过，也在 BentoML 做过资深 MLOps 工程师。9 月 23 日，他发布了菜单栏工具 Magpie。一周就有 3000 多 Star，现在已经超过 2.4 万，几乎每天都在连着发版。 Magpie 解决的是同时用几个 Agent 改配置太麻烦的问题。哪个 Agent 正在用哪个模型，在菜单栏里点一下就能换，背后的本地网关会把几家不同的 API 协议实时互译。 Magpie 还能共享订阅。你在某个 Agent 里登录过 Claude Pro 或者 ChatGPT Plus，这份订阅就能拿给其他 Agent 一起用。它还会在本地回放真实的调用记录，算出什么时候压缩上下文最省 Token。 yetone 有句话说得很直接，「Agent 时代，模型之间差距没有想象中大，Harness 的差距才是真的，一切 Infra 都值得为 Agent 重新写一遍。」 Jason Young：改配置太麻烦，催生了一个近 15 万 Star 的项目 项目：https://www.ccswitch.io/ 说到 Magpie，国内社区最常拿来跟它比的，是 CC Switch。去年 8 月上线以来，这个基于 Tauri 2 和 Rust 的跨平台桌面工具，已经在 GitHub 上攒下了近 15 万颗 Star 和 9800 多次 Fork。 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI、OpenCode 各有一套 API Key、接口地址和模型配置，要在不同供应商、中转服务之间来回切换，只能手动改文件。CC Switch 把这些都放进了一个界面里，一键就能切换，MCP、Prompts、Skills 也能统一管理，在各家花了多少钱也看得清楚。 JoyWong：给 Agent 当监工，还卖起了角色和声音 项目：https://agentbell.dev/ 同时开着几个窗口让 Agent 干活时，人总得时不时切回去看一眼进度。JoyWong 做的 AgentBell 是一个 macOS 菜单栏应用，专门替你盯着这几个工具里 Agent 的状态。 任务跑完了、出错了、在等你确认，或者半天没动静，它都会在菜单栏提醒你，桌面上的小角色也会跳出来喊你，还能用语音播报出来。Agent 闲下来的时候，它就给你播几条 AI 和科技新闻。 它收费的地方也挺有意思，卖的是角色和声音，比如温柔治愈的 Hiyori、暴躁码农疯狂兔子、黑客风的码猫。一个效率工具，顺手做起了陪伴。 idoubi：裸辞两年上线 20 多款产品，这次给 Agent 做了个「微信」 项目：https://github.com/thinkany-ai/douchat idoubi 在腾讯做过五年后台开发。2023 年裸辞后，他在两年多里一口气上线了 20 多款产品，包括 AI 搜索 ThinkAny、月访问量峰值 270 万的 MCP 应用市场 MCP.so，以及预售四小时破万美元的 SaaS 模板 ShipAny，还写了一本《这就是 MCP》。 今年 10 月，他开源了新作品 douchat，定位是「Agent 版微信」。它会自动找出你电脑上的 Codex、Claude Code 等本地 Agent，把它们变成可以拉进群的「联系人」。你、你的同事，还有你们各自的 Agent，可以待在同一个群里讨论、派活，共享同一份上下文。 同期，他还开源了连接器平台 Connany，五分钟内帮任意 Agent 统一接上 Notion 与 GitHub 等 25 个外部服务。 benn：让人和不同的 Agent 共享同一段对话 项目：https://sumus.im/ benn 也是前腾讯高级工程师。他之前一个人做出了 AI 客户端 Chatbox，在 GitHub 上拿到 4 万多 Star，后来产品被收购。从做出来到卖出去，一个独立产品能走的路，他已经完整走过一遍了。 他的新产品 Sumus 从 9 月开始公测，想解决的问题是，你调好了一个很好用的 Agent，想让朋友、同事也一起用，该怎么办？分享配置或模板是一种办法，但之前聊过的内容、积累下来的上下文，都带不过去。 Sumus 的做法，是把人、云端 Agent 和本地 Agent 都拉进同一段对话。云端 Agent 负责查资料、做规划，本地 Agent 负责写代码、执行。所有人都能在同一个对话流里继续追问、补充上下文。 更多阅读 Manus 内部复盘：一家 Agent 公司，如何先用 Agent 改造自己？ 对话K2 Lab王铭：Muse帮人省钱，Moras帮人赚钱，这才是垂直赛道Personal AI的刚需 聊Agent商业化、做AI产品、链接全球资源，近期这些活动别错过 items.content: 聊Agent商业化、做AI产品、链接全球资源，近期这些活动别错过 AI system Social Agent 极客公园 2026-10-28 23:40 分享 以下文章来源于mp.weixin.qq.com 想探索 Agent 时代的新商业模式、带着 AI 产品寻找合作机会，或者和全球一线 AI 工程师交流？10 月至 11 月，北京、上海、新加坡和旧金山都有值得关注的活 动。从 Idea Rush、创业路演到 AI 技术大会，一起看看有哪些新机会。 此外，我们还整理了近期值得参与的一些活动，对更多活动感兴趣的小伙伴，可以点击文末的 「阅读原文」 查看。 Agent 杀死 SaaS？新的机会在哪里？｜Idea Rush 主办方： Founder Park 活动时间： 11 月 7 日 活动地点： 北京朝阳区 活动主题： 新一期 Idea Rush，我们打算进一步聊点更实际的，Agent 时代的产品/服务怎么获客、收费，以及新的商业模式在哪里？尤其是近期 REA（Reverse Engineer Anything）这一波火起来之后，越来越多的开源替代方案出来了。但产品真的能被重做吗？随之的生意也能被重做吗？ 活动人群： 正在探索 AI 产品或开源项目的商业化 正在用 AI 重做传统软件，或开发开源替代方案 正在做 To B / SaaS 产品，寻找客户或验证 PMF 从事 FDE、企业 AI 落地或定制化交付，有一线经验 对 AI 软件行业的增长获客、定价、商业化等有实践经验和独特想法 活动玩法： 所有人都要参与，并选择你的角色： 分享者：带着你的 idea 来，大家一起帮你盖楼；盖楼者，带着你的经验和想法来，帮别人盖好楼 活动报名 ： https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/1copTYZZCf-vKjdi60eCHQ AGI Playground Founder Show @Singapore 主办方： Founder Park 活动时间： 10 月 30 日 活动地点： 新加坡 活动亮点： 8 支团队，每队 15 分钟路演 + 5 分钟互动 台下会有全球投资人、创业者、企业/生态伙伴、研究员和大厂战略团队 除了路演，还有 Open Mic & Networking，聊产品、找合作、认识同行 如果你正在做一个面向全球市场的 AI 产品，已经上线或有可运行 Demo，欢迎带来现场讲。 路演报名： https://geek.feishu.cn/share/base/form/shrcn7ua2DQpye5e7pvo8gLebve 观众报名： https://luma.com/yevjd99y 叠加态之夜 · 首次线下分享会 主办方： 叠加态社区 Superposition 活动时间： 10 月 30 日 活动地点： 北京·798 艺术区（报名筛选通过后，入群告知具体地点） 活动亮点： 量子计算 × 具身智能的哈希碰撞 当量子计算撞上 Physical AI，会碰出什么新的计算范式？ 两场硬核 Talk、一场灵感圆桌、一顿边吃边聊的晚餐。 现场更有来自智元、minimax、谋先飞、玻色量子等专家沟通交流 报名方式 ： https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/CWn0Px9RN7kRQ2y4KfOUCg 从开源创新到全球增长｜发布开放日暨优质项目路演 主办方： Praxis 增长加速器 活动时间： 10 月 30 日 活动地点： 上海张江 AI 应用商店（上海市海科路 1650 号） 活动亮点： Praxis 线下加速器基地，终于要和大家见面了啦，开源中国×Praxis 联合打造的【开物基地 OPENLAND】即将发布。 在「从开源创新到全球增长」开放日现场，旗舰基地计划将重磅官宣，同时 2026 上海开源软件应用创新大赛总决赛也将在这里举办，这次不只聊经验，也通过真实项目验证经验、链接资本，并认识更多新朋友。 开放日亮点： 10 大优质项目路演 2 堂增长实战课 3 小时晚间开放麦 活动报名： https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/9UvHRsob83RUKPW4MkuxVQ AI Engineer Shanghai 2026 主办方： AI Engineer 活动时间： 11 月 5- 6 日 活动地点： 上海虹桥祥源希尔顿酒店 活动亮点： 在上海和中美 AI 大咖面对面：硅谷当红 AI Engineer 大会来到上海，汇聚全球一线 AI builders—— 【见大咖】与 Latent Space 的 Swyx，以及来自 Cursor、World Labs、Arena、HeyGen、Gemini 等前沿 AI 团队的嘉宾面对面交流！ 【听实战】从 Agent 构建、模型选型到产品落地，听一线实践者分享真实经验，直击技术难点，现场看 Demo。 【找商机】汇聚 AI 创业者、CTO 与一线工程师，带着你的项目和问题来，链接志同道合的伙伴，探索合作机会。 完整议程： https://ai.engineer/shanghai/2026 活动报名： https://aie.anruicloud.com/pay?track=FounderPark GTC2026 全球流量大会（上海） 主办方： 白鲸出海 活动时间： 11 月 4 日 -5 日 活动地点： 上海世博展览馆 H3 馆 活动亮点： 跨境出海人的年度盛会来了！GTC2026 Shanghai 将于 11 月 4-5 日在上海世博展览馆 H3 馆举办！ 4 大主题峰会，聚焦游戏/应用/技术/品牌 5000+同行齐聚，拓展高端人脉 120+展商，一站式解决流量与资源难题 FP 社区福利免费票，分论坛+两日展区畅行~ 活动报名： https://baijing.cn/ieQvm SGLang Summit 主办方： SGLang 活动时间： 11 月 12-13 日 活动地点： 旧金山 活动亮点： 两天预计有 2000+ 人参会、100+ 位嘉宾、50+ 场分享。陈立武、翁荔、Thinking Machines CTO Soumith、Perplexity CEO Aravind、田渊栋、焦剑涛等重磅嘉宾将到场，还有来自 OpenAI, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, AWS, MiniMax 等前沿科技公司的资深研究员和工程师同台交流。 从大厂到新锐 AI 团队，平时关注的人和公司，都能现场见到！大家将围绕 Agent 与软件开发、下一代模型、AI 应用落地、机器人与世界模型、生成式媒体、递归自我改进（RSI）、强化学习、芯片和基础设施展开分享。现场还有 GPU 和公司展台、workshop，以及各种社交娱乐活动，方便大家当面交流。 活动报名 ：https://sglang.io/summit NbN Founder Meetup · 杭州万圣节「幽灵船长与增长引擎」 主办方： NextbyNEXT 活动时间： 10 月 31 日 活动地点： 杭州 活动形式： 嘉宾分享 ｜ 所有人破冰交流 ｜万圣节下午茶/晚餐 ｜抽奖 活动报名： https://hdxu.cn/iJ7qk 更多活动详情介绍，⬇️点击「阅读原文」 更多阅读 做产品没有门槛之后：1083 个 AI Native 创业者教给我们的事 闭门分享精华：ToB 出海美国，别急着复制国内打法 Personal AI 都在谈的「意图捕获」，可能是今天企业级 Agent 最需要的 REA 能逆向产品，但它能逆向一门生意吗？ 转载原创文章请添加微信：founderparker 内容中包含的图片若涉及版权问题，请及时与我们联系删除 点赞 收藏 评论 分享到Link 举报反馈 举报类型（必选） 样式问题 涉嫌广告 内容抄袭 内容侵权 政治相关 内容涉黄 其他 items.title: Flint-interactive: A language for creating interactive data visualizations
items.summary: At a glance Brings rich interactivity to AI-generated charts: Flint-interactive enables agents to create data visualizations that users can explore directly through clicking, filtering, zooming, highlighting, and cross-chart interactions. Makes complex interactions easier to build: Instead of requiring low-level visualization code, Flint-interactive lets users and agents define behaviors using high-level semantic events and update operators. Improves reliability and reduces development effort: By using Flint’s compiler to handle interaction logic and visual dependencies, the system helps avoid many of the layout, rendering, and debugging challenges common in custom interactive visualizations. Connects charts, text, tables, and applications: Flint-interactive supports interactive data stories, dashboards, and connected experiences where actions in one view can update charts, documents, widgets, or application state in another. AI agents make it easy to analyze data and generate reports
items.content: At a glance Brings rich interactivity to AI-generated charts: Flint-interactive enables agents to create data visualizations that users can explore directly through clicking, filtering, zooming, highlighting, and cross-chart interactions. Makes complex interactions easier to build: Instead of requiring low-level visualization code, Flint-interactive lets users and agents define behaviors using high-level semantic events and update operators. Improves reliability and reduces development effort: By using Flint’s compiler to handle interaction logic and visual dependencies, the system helps avoid many of the layout, rendering, and debugging challenges common in custom interactive visualizations. Connects charts, text, tables, and applications: Flint-interactive supports interactive data stories, dashboards, and connected experiences where actions in one view can update charts, documents, widgets, or application state in another. AI agents make it easy to analyze data and generate reports with data visualizations. They help users examine patterns more efficiently than by reading verbose text. However, when we’re feeling exploratory, we want to go beyond static visualizations. : We want to interact with charts to zoom in on details, compare data across charts, or even highlight related text in the document from a chart selection, and vice versa. This requires agents to be able to create interactive data visualizations that communicate information while letting readers explore beyond the author’s chosen view, ideally with the quality of interactive stories in sophisticated data journalism. This leaves us wondering: (As a user) Can I interact with charts directly in chat to explore the data and ask follow-up questions based on what I select? (As a developer) Can I enable the AI agents I build for my customers to generate interactive visualizations that help them explore and understand their data? Yes, it’s possible, but there is a significant practical gap. Even with capable frontier models, we still face: High generation cost. Agents rarely produce a fully satisfactory interactive visualization in one turn. Repeated rounds of reasoning, coding, and debugging consume tokens and time. Reliability. Interactive visualizations are challenging enough that expressive interactive charts introduce poor layouts or broken interactions easily, and we risk introducing new problems when trying to fix them. These challenges help explain why consistently generating high-quality interactive visualizations remain difficult in real-world use. Meanwhile, built-in interactions in some visualization libraries are not expressive enough on their own to create bespoke interactive charts. And these challenges are results of the lack of an expressive yet high-level language to specify visual interactions. Microsoft Research StorY OptiMind: When the system meets the floor A three‑month pilot in a Midwestern bottling plant shows what happens when AI moves beyond chat and into decision-making, where constraints shift, stakes are real, and answers must hold. Learn more Opens in a new tab Flint-interactive Flint-interactive (opens in new tab) is a language for creating interactive data visualizations on top of Flint. It allows users to create dashboards, data stories, and interactive artifacts more easily. The power of Flint-interactive comes from Flint’s compiler, which translates user interactions into semantic events that capture the meaning behind what users select. It then uses high-level operators to update visualizations in response to those events, making sophisticated interactions far easier to create and maintain. This shifts the heavy burden of resolving complex dependencies between interaction and visual logic to the compiler, so the user (or the agent) can easily describe expressive interactions with high-level specifications. Example 1: We can enable the user to brush one visual view, and the chart highlights all groups of country selected by the user with a simple preset interaction linked-brush. How to use 1. Use Flint in your chat Use Flint Interactive directly in your chat or canvas environment through Flint-MCP and MCP Apps, following the MCP setup guide. With the latest release, tell your agent what to chart and which interactions you want; it can generate an interaction_spec alongside the Flint chart spec and render the interactive chart in your conversation. Example 2: Using Flint-interactive in the chat environment, allowing the agent to produce interactive charts more reliably with simple Flint specifications. It also enables the user to select and pass context to the follow-up turns. 2. Build an interactive app with Flint Build interactive charts in a dashboard, data story, or other application with Flint Interactive Canvas. Your app can use event handlers to process semantic events emitted by Flint Canvas, for example to filter a table, update another chart, or change application state. To let your app’s widgets control how the chart updates, send update operators to Flint Canvas. Example 2: Flint-interactive allows developers to define interactions between charts and external elements (e.g., table, paragraph). Here, the user can click the table to highlight points in the chart and verse versa. 3. Create bespoke interactions To create bespoke interactions beyond Flint’s presets, define a trigger and a custom handle function with the programming API that maps semantic events to custom chart update sequences. For example, a handler can highlight a clicked country and label it by name. It combines set-style and set-annotation without manipulating renderer-specific marks. Example 4: The agent can create bespoke interactive visualizations with Flint’s programming API. In this DimpVis example, the user can drag the point along the time path to visualize how all cities’ temperature and precipitation changes. How it works Flint Canvas is a state machine that tracks user interactions on the canvas and manages visual rendering state. Flint makes interaction specification easy by separating visual logic, managed by the compiler, from interaction logic, specified by the user at the semantic level: Visual logic: The compiler automatically resolves raw triggers, such as clicks, drags, and key presses, into semantic events that identify chart elements and data. It also translates update operators into rendered canvas changes, handling hit testing, and low-level visual updates. Interaction logic: The user specifies interactions by mapping semantic interaction events to chart update operators, such as set style to highlight data, set annotation to label a point, or set viewport to pan or zoom. The user can also use those semantic events to update external tables, widgets, or application states. Figure 1: Flint interactive allows the agent to describe interaction logic by mapping “what semantic event is the user interacting with” to “what updates they want for the canvas surface”. The compiler takes the heavy lifting of resolving visual updates and manages the runtime, which makes interaction authoring more reliable c and cost effective. This separation means users do not need to reverse-engineer rendering logic or manipulate renderer-specific marks, making interactions easier to specify and maintain. Furthermore, because event generation and visual updates are compositional, the same model also connects Flint with tables, text, other charts, and widgets to build interactive stories and dashboards. Try it now! Video playback requires cookie consent Chart users: Set up Flint in your chat (opens in new tab) and ask your agent to create an interactive chart. Find inspiration in the interaction gallery. App builders: Build interactive dashboards, data stories, and connected views with the programming API (opens in new tab) . Share the interaction-author skill with your coding agent to add presets to your app. Interaction designers: Explore the bespoke examples (opens in new tab) , design a new interaction, and turn it into a reusable preset. Propose a preset on GitHub and share your prototype or implementation to help expand Flint’s interaction vocabulary. items.content: Data Center / Cloud Build a Validated Kubernetes Runtime for NVIDIA Dynamo Oct 30, 2026 By Stefan Schimanski , Jamie Li and Yuan Chen Like Discuss (0) L T F R E AI-Generated Summary NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform packages NVIDIA Dynamo and its supporting infrastructure into validated recipes through NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR). AICR captures runtime requirements such as GPU driver stacks, Dynamic Resource Allocation, gang scheduling, node health signals, and Prometheus metrics in reproducible recipes with pinned component versions. Dynamo 1.4.2 uses TCP for the request plane and ZMQ for KV-cache events, enabling both the native Dynamo Frontend router and the Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE) / Endpoint Picker Plugin (EPP) path to make cache-aware routing decisions. The Dynamo Frontend router path suits model-specific endpoints with the smallest serving topology, while the GAIE/EPP path integrates with shared Kubernetes ingress managed through Gateway API resources. AICR separates runtime setup from application deployment through a five-step flow: snapshot the cluster, generate a Dynamo inference recipe, render a deployment bundle, deploy the runtime with Helmfile or GitOps, and validate the installed runtime before installing application workloads. Next Steps Explore the NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) to configure and validate inference infrastructure. Explore the NVIDIA Dynamo repository for the distributed inference framework. Join the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Slack community for discussion and hands-on workshops. Powered by NVIDIA Nemotron. AI-generated content may summarize information incompletely. Verify important information. Learn more Teams building AI applications need a repeatable path from a model configuration to a working inference endpoint. NVIDIA Dynamo is a distributed inference framework that coordinates model serving across GPU workers. Deploying it on Kubernetes is only a first step. A successful model deployment requires more: GPU drivers, resource allocation, scheduling, networking, and monitoring must all work together. Resolving these dependencies takes time away from testing model behavior, serving performance, and application integration. The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform brings together technologies to help the ecosystem design, build, and operate more efficient AI factories, and Dynamo is one of them. To make management of those infrastructure dependencies easier, the platform contains NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR). It packages NVIDIA Dynamo and its supporting infrastructure into validated recipes. Each recipe defines a configuration for a specific environment and workload, including pinned component versions, compatibility constraints, and validation checks. AICR gives platform teams a repeatable way to deploy and check the runtime, providing developers with a consistent foundation for serving models and testing applications. This walkthrough covers the infrastructure that supports Dynamo on Kubernetes, compares two routing options, and shows how to deploy and validate the runtime with AICR. Why the underlying runtime matters for Dynamo Running a model with Dynamo on Kubernetes starts with a DynamoGraphDeployment that specifies how vLLM , SGLang , or NVIDIA TensorRT LLM should run in pods on the cluster. But the graph is only the top of the stack. A production inference cluster also needs a runtime layer below it. It has to answer questions like: Is the NVIDIA GPU Operator installed with a driver stack that matches the nodes? Are GPU nodes labeled and discoverable? Does the cluster expose GPUs through the expected Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) driver? Can the scheduler place GPU workers with the required topology and gang scheduling semantics? Are node health signals available before workloads land on a degraded node? Is Prometheus reachable for Dynamo and accelerator metrics? Is the Gateway API / Endpoint Picker (EPP) path configured when the deployment should be Kubernetes-native at ingress? AICR captures these runtime requirements in the recipe. What AICR ships for Dynamo An AICR Dynamo recipe packages both Dynamo and the cluster runtime components it depends on. AICR ships version 1.4.2 of the dynamo-platform chart, which includes the Dynamo operator, Dynamo runtime images, and resources such as the nvidia.com/v1beta1 DynamoGraphDeployment CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) . v1beta1 replaces the former v1alpha1 API version. Table 1 lists the supporting infrastructure components included in the recipe. Prerequisite Requirement Component in the AICR recipe GPU driver stack Driver and GPU software stack that matches the nodes NVIDIA GPU Operator GPU discovery GPU nodes labeled and discoverable for placement Node Feature Discovery GPU allocation GPUs exposed through Kubernetes-native Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) DRA Driver for NVIDIA GPUs Scheduling GPU workers placed with the required topology and gang scheduling KAI Scheduler Inference Workload Orchestration Multi-component serving graphs started, placed, and scaled as coordinated groups Grove Node health Health signals available before workloads land on a degraded node NVSentinel and Nodewright , where supported by the selected recipe Metrics Cluster, accelerator, and Dynamo service metrics collected Prometheus stack Ingress Gateway / EPP path configured when ingress is Kubernetes-native agentgateway and Gateway API resources, described in the routing sections Table 1. Runtime prerequisites below Dynamo and the components the AICR recipe installs for each In addition, the recipe pins component versions and records configuration values, node selectors, tolerations, checksums, and validation expectations to make deployment reproducible. With Dynamo 1.4, frontends, workers, optional Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE) / Endpoint Picker Plugin (EPP) components , and other Dynamo services discover each other through Kubernetes resources. AICR’s default path therefore no longer uses NATS, and the dynamo-platform chart no longer installs it by default. NATS remains available as an opt-in for deployments that need it. Agentic workloads repeatedly extend long token prefixes, including system prompts, tool definitions, conversation history, and tool results. If a turn reaches a worker without that prefix in GPU memory, the system reprocesses intermediate tokens instead of reusing cached results. Dynamo routes requests to workers that already hold the relevant KV blocks, either through its frontend router or through GAIE/EPP integration at the Gateway API layer. Dynamo can also separate prompt processing (prefill) from token generation (decode), an architecture known as disaggregated serving. On KV-cache misses, all or part of the prompt must be reprocessed by the prefill pool. Decode workers then take over token-by-token generation, which has different GPU, memory, latency, and batching characteristics. The cache miss rate depends on the workload. Long-running agentic sessions behave differently from one-off chat requests. Disaggregated serving enables operators to scale and tune prefill and decode capacity independently for a given request mix. The request plane and KV-cache event plane are separate. In Dynamo 1.4.2, the default AICR Kubernetes path uses TCP for requests and ZMQ for KV-cache events. Each vLLM worker engine emits raw KV-cache events through a local ZMQ publisher, for example, with the following vLLM configuration: --enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config \ {"enable_kv_cache_events": true, "publisher": "zmq", "endpoint": "tcp://*:5557"} Dynamo’s worker runtime then subscribes to that local vLLM event source, normalizes the events, and republishes them onto the Dynamo event plane. Both the native Dynamo Frontend router and the GAIE/EPP path use this Dynamo-managed KV-cache state to make routing decisions. What are the Dynamo routing paths on Kubernetes? Dynamo supports two routing paths on Kubernetes. The first uses the Dynamo Frontend router for worker selection. The second uses a Kubernetes Gateway API implementation for ingress and Dynamo EPP for endpoint selection. AICR ships and validates the Dynamo runtime for either topology. Path 1: Dynamo Frontend router The default path exposes a Dynamo Frontend behind a Kubernetes Service. Running with DYN_ROUTER_MODE=kv , the Frontend tokenizes each request, scores eligible workers using prefix overlap and current load, selects a worker, and dispatches the request through the Dynamo request plane, which uses TCP by default. This path is suitable when an application team owns a model-specific endpoint or an existing edge proxy only needs to forward traffic to the Dynamo Frontend Service. It is the smallest topology for deploying and validating a Dynamo graph and is the most production-proven serving option. It does not require the additional gateway and EPP components used in Path 2. Figure 1. The Dynamo Frontend selects a vLLM worker based on KV-cache overlap and load. Requests use the TCP request plane; worker KV-cache events reach the Frontend through the ZMQ-backed event plane Path 2: Gateway API Inference Extension and Dynamo EPP This path integrates Dynamo with the Gateway API and Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE). In the AICR example, agentgateway resolves an HTTPRoute to an InferencePool . The Dynamo operator creates that InferencePool from the DynamoGraphDeployment : its selector identifies eligible worker pods, while its endpointPickerRef identifies the Dynamo EPP Service. The gateway invokes the Dynamo EPP through GAIE’s endpoint-selection interface. The EPP tokenizes the request and uses Dynamo’s KV router to select an endpoint. It returns the selection and routing metadata to the gateway implementation, which is the actual HTTP proxy. In this mode, each routable worker pod includes a Dynamo Frontend sidecar that receives the request from the gateway and forwards it to the local worker container. The Frontend runs with --router-mode direct , so it applies the EPP selection without rerouting. This path is suitable when the platform team manages shared Kubernetes ingress and needs to configure model endpoint worker selection, timeouts, retries, and fallback through Gateway API mechanisms. Note that both routing approaches can work behind a Gateway API HTTPRoute . The difference is which component manages the transport to the worker: the Dynamo Frontend or the Gateway itself. Note: This post covers Dynamo’s operator-managed DynamoGraphDeployment integration with GAIE; the experimental standalone vanilla vLLM on-ramp is a separate integration. In Dynamo 1.4, this path uses GAIE’s Go EPP framework with Dynamo’s Rust KV router embedded through CGO and configured through eppConfig . Outlook: Starting with Dynamo 1.5, a native Rust EPP replaces the Go/CGO bridge. It implements GAIE’s Lightweight Endpoint Picker ( ext_proc ) interface directly, runs the full Dynamo router in-process, and uses DYN_* environment variables in place of the eppConfig plugin and scheduling profiles. Aggregated and disaggregated routing are handled directly from the worker roles registered through Dynamo discovery. The surrounding Kubernetes topology remains unchanged. Removing the Go plugin framework and CGO boundary also reduces per-request EPP overhead. Figure 2. The GAIE / EPP path delegates the worker network transport to the Gateway while Dynamo performs KV-aware endpoint selection A client request enters through a gateway, such as agentgateway, and matches an HTTPRoute backed by an InferencePool . The Gateway invokes the Dynamo EPP, which performs just the token-aware KV selection and returns the selected endpoint and routing metadata. The Gateway then forwards the request to the selected worker’s Frontend sidecar in direct mode, which sends it to the vLLM worker over the Dynamo request plane. Worker KV-cache state reaches the EPP through the Dynamo event plane, while the Dynamo operator creates the EPP and InferencePool from the DynamoGraphDeployment . Table 2 compares the Dynamo Frontend and Gateway API/EPP paths. Decision Dynamo Router GAIE / EPP Ingress owner Dynamo Frontend Service Gateway and HTTPRoute Worker selection The Frontend selects and dispatches to a worker The EPP selects an endpoint; the Gateway forwards the request Request path Client → Frontend → worker Client → Gateway → worker Frontend sidecar → worker Best fit A model-specific Dynamo endpoint with the smallest serving topology A shared Kubernetes ingress managed through Gateway API resources Additional infrastructure None beyond the Dynamo frontend and workers GAIE-compatible Gateway, InferencePool, EPP, and worker frontend sidecars KV-cache behavior Dynamo KV-aware routing from worker-published cache and load state The same Dynamo KV-aware routing at the Gateway layer Table 2. Decision criteria for the Dynamo router and GAIE / EPP routing paths Both paths use worker-published KV-cache events for precise cache-aware placement. The runtime bundle is then rendered, deployed, and validated before the application’s DynamoGraphDeployment is installed and its inference endpoints are tested. Step 1: Snapshot the cluster The snapshot captures the cluster state that AICR uses for recipe selection and validation: aicr snapshot \ --namespace aicr-validation \ --output snapshot.yaml When no placement flags are specified, AICR automatically targets nodes labeled nvidia.com/gpu.present=true and tolerates GPU-node taints. The --node-selector and --toleration flags provide more specific placement when required by the cluster. Step 2: Generate the Dynamo inference recipe AICR uses the snapshot to identify the Kubernetes distribution, GPU accelerator, and GPU-node operating system. The command specifies the workload intent and platform: aicr recipe \ --snapshot snapshot.yaml \ --intent inference \ --platform dynamo \ --output recipe.yaml The generated recipe records pinned component versions, environment-specific configuration, compatibility constraints, and validation checks. Helm chart versions for the AICR v1.0.0 Amazon EKS Dynamo inference recipe The AICR team tested these component versions together on the specified platforms and hardware. The following validation steps verify that the cluster meets the selected recipe’s requirements. Optional offline check Recipe selection already uses the cluster facts in snapshot.yaml , so validating the generated recipe against that same snapshot adds little. Offline validation is useful when testing a recipe against a different captured cluster snapshot without contacting Kubernetes. It evaluates declarative constraints, while behavioral checks are reported as skipped. aicr validate \ --recipe recipe.yaml \ --snapshot candidate-snapshot.yaml \ --no-cluster \ --output dry-run.json Step 3: Render the runtime bundle AICR renders the recipe into deployment-ready Helm values and manifests: aicr bundle \ --recipe recipe.yaml \ --accelerated-node-selector nodeGroup=gpu-worker \ --accelerated-node-toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoSchedule \ --accelerated-node-toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoExecute \ --system-node-selector nodeGroup=system-worker \ --system-node-toleration dedicated=system-workload:NoSchedule \ --system-node-toleration dedicated=system-workload:NoExecute \ --set-json agentgateway:allowedSourceRanges='["<your-cidr>"]' \ --deployer helmfile \ --output bundle These placement flags reflect the test cluster used for this walkthrough. The flags can be adapted or omitted for clusters with different labels and taints. If the cluster has no default StorageClass, the command also requires --storage-class . Step 4: Deploy the runtime For a local deployment without an in-cluster GitOps controller, Helmfile provides a deployment option. With Helm and the helm-diff plugin available locally, the following commands inspect the AICR-generated release graph before applying it: helmfile -f bundle/helmfile.yaml diff helmfile -f bundle/helmfile.yaml apply AICR encodes component dependencies in the generated Helmfile bundle. Helmfile processes those dependency tiers in order and applies independent components within a tier concurrently. Rerunning apply reconciles the installed Helm releases with the generated configuration. If Helmfile is not available, the bundle can be regenerated with AICR’s default Helm deployer. Its generated deploy.sh script is a lightweight fallback for an interactive test drive: aicr bundle \ --recipe recipe.yaml \ [... all the flags setting node selectors and tolerations ...] \ --set-json agentgateway:allowedSourceRanges='["<your-cidr>"]' \ --deployer helm \ --output bundle-helm chmod +x bundle-helm/deploy.sh ./bundle-helm/deploy.sh For production, AICR also renders GitOps bundles with --deployer argocd , --deployer argocd-helm , and --deployer flux . Step 5: Validate the installed runtime After installation, deployment and conformance validation check the live cluster before the application workload is installed. Because no snapshot is supplied here, AICR captures the current cluster state before running the validator Jobs. aicr validate \ --recipe recipe.yaml \ --node-selector nodeGroup=gpu-worker \ --toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoSchedule \ --toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoExecute \ --phase deployment \ --phase conformance \ --output report.json The application DynamoGraphDeployment is installed only after these checks pass. Performance validation runs separately because it deploys a temporary serving workload and consumes the GPUs under test. What does AICR validation check? AICR validates the installed runtime against the checks and constraints encoded in the selected recipe. Checks vary by recipe. For a Dynamo inference recipe, deployment and conformance validation typically cover the following: Area What is checked Cluster baseline Expected cluster resources, GPU allocatable capacity, and a functional nvidia-smi on accelerator nodes Platform health GPU Operator health and version, plus Dynamo platform and operator health Accelerator access DRA support and secure accelerator access Scheduling and scaling Gang scheduling, pod autoscaling, cluster autoscaling, and robust controller behavior Observability Prometheus-backed accelerator and AI service metrics Ingress Gateway API and agentgateway readiness for Kubernetes-native ingress Table 4. Deployment and conformance checks for an AICR Dynamo recipe These checks verify that the installed runtime meets the selected recipe’s requirements before an application is deployed. AICR combines a versioned runtime configuration with checks that verify whether the cluster meets the selected recipe’s requirements. Teams deploying Dynamo on Kubernetes can use AICR’s recipes and deployment examples to configure, deploy, and validate the infrastructure supporting their inference workload. Additional projects and community resources are available through the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory GitHub . Discussion is available in the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Slack community. The NVIDIA DSX OS AI Inference and Contributor Workshop provides hands-on experience with AICR during KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America. Registration is required, as seating is limited. The NVIDIA booth #170 at KubeCon features Kubernetes deep dives and live demos. The following validation steps verify that the cluster meets the selected recipe’s requirements. Optional offline check Recipe selection already uses the cluster facts in snapshot.yaml , so validating the generated recipe against that same snapshot adds little. Offline validation is useful when testing a recipe against a different captured cluster snapshot without contacting Kubernetes. It evaluates declarative constraints, while behavioral checks are reported as skipped. aicr validate \ --recipe recipe.yaml \ --snapshot candidate-snapshot.yaml \ --no-cluster \ --output dry-run.json Step 3: Render the runtime bundle AICR renders the recipe into deployment-ready Helm values and manifests: aicr bundle \ --recipe recipe.yaml \ --accelerated-node-selector nodeGroup=gpu-worker \ --accelerated-node-toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoSchedule \ --accelerated-node-toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoExecute \ --system-node-selector nodeGroup=system-worker \ --system-node-toleration dedicated=system-workload:NoSchedule \ --system-node-toleration dedicated=system-workload:NoExecute \ --set-json agentgateway:allowedSourceRanges='["<your-cidr>"]' \ --deployer helmfile \ --output bundle These placement flags reflect the test cluster used for this walkthrough. The flags can be adapted or omitted for clusters with different labels and taints. If the cluster has no default StorageClass, the command also requires --storage-class . Step 4: Deploy the runtime For a local deployment without an in-cluster GitOps controller, Helmfile provides a deployment option. With Helm and the helm-diff plugin available locally, the following commands inspect the AICR-generated release graph before applying it: helmfile -f bundle/helmfile.yaml diff helmfile -f bundle/helmfile.yaml apply AICR encodes component dependencies in the generated Helmfile bundle. Helmfile processes those dependency tiers in order and applies independent components within a tier concurrently. Rerunning apply reconciles the installed Helm releases with the generated configuration. If Helmfile is not available, the bundle can be regenerated with AICR’s default Helm deployer. Its generated deploy.sh script is a lightweight fallback for an interactive test drive: aicr bundle \ --recipe recipe.yaml \ [... all the flags setting node selectors and tolerations ...] \ --set-json agentgateway:allowedSourceRanges='["<your-cidr>"]' \ --deployer helm \ --output bundle-helm chmod +x bundle-helm/deploy.sh ./bundle-helm/deploy.sh For production, AICR also renders GitOps bundles with --deployer argocd , --deployer argocd-helm , and --deployer flux . Step 5: Validate the installed runtime After installation, deployment and conformance validation check the live cluster before the application workload is installed. Because no snapshot is supplied here, AICR captures the current cluster state before running the validator Jobs. aicr validate \ --recipe recipe.yaml \ --node-selector nodeGroup=gpu-worker \ --toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoSchedule \ --toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoExecute \ --phase deployment \ --phase conformance \ --output report.json The application DynamoGraphDeployment is installed only after these checks pass. Performance validation runs separately because it deploys a temporary serving workload and consumes the GPUs under test. What does AICR validation check? AICR validates the installed runtime against the checks and constraints encoded in the selected recipe. Checks vary by recipe. For a Dynamo inference recipe, deployment and conformance validation typically cover the following: Area What is checked Cluster baseline Expected cluster resources, GPU allocatable capacity, and a functional nvidia-smi on accelerator nodes Platform health GPU Operator health and version, plus Dynamo platform and operator health Accelerator access DRA support and secure accelerator access Scheduling and scaling Gang scheduling, pod autoscaling, cluster autoscaling, and robust controller behavior Observability Prometheus-backed accelerator and AI service metrics Ingress Gateway API and agentgateway readiness for Kubernetes-native ingress Table 4. Deployment and conformance checks for an AICR Dynamo recipe These checks verify that the installed runtime meets the selected recipe’s requirements before an application is deployed. AICR combines a versioned runtime configuration with checks that verify whether the cluster meets the selected recipe’s requirements. Get Started NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) and NVIDIA Dynamo are open-source components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform. Teams deploying Dynamo on Kubernetes can use AICR’s recipes and deployment examples to configure, deploy, and validate the infrastructure supporting their inference workload. Additional projects and community resources are available through the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory GitHub . Discussion is available in the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Slack community. The NVIDIA DSX OS AI Inference and Contributor Workshop provides hands-on experience with AICR during KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America. Registration is required, as seating is limited. The NVIDIA booth #170 at KubeCon features Kubernetes deep dives and live demos. items.content: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.40578 (cs) [Submitted on 29 Oct 2026] Title: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents Authors: Qiushi Sun , Da Yu , Alexander Knop , Amer Sinha , Lingpeng Kong , Ben Kao , Ravi Kumar , Pritish Kamath View a PDF of the paper titled VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents, by Qiushi Sun and 7 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Building and scaling computer-using agents (CUAs) across desktop, mobile, and web environments requires reliable task-completion verification for data curation, evaluation, and reinforcement learning. Typical automated approaches prompt vision-language models (VLMs) to judge trajectories or generate programs to inspect application state. However, both rely on partial views of complex digital environments. VLM judges are restricted to supplied observations, while generated programs depend on accessible state. These views can omit decisive evidence or leave completion judgments unsupported. Tailoring separate verifiers to different platforms and access settings adds further engineering cost. We present VeriCUA, a platform-agnostic framework for verification through agentic exploration. It treats verification as dynamic evidence gathering and assessment within a shared procedure for online and offline settings across platforms and observation modalities. After inspecting the available context to construct a task rubric, the verifier selects GUI or code checks for unresolved requirements and combines their findings under explicit evidence rules. Experiments show improved agreement with reference labels over the compared baselines across these settings, with the largest offline gains on hard cases and stronger rejection of false completion claims online. Further analyses connect these gains to complementary evidence and test-time exploration. items.content: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents Qiushi Sun Affiliation: Google Da Yu Affiliation: Google Alexander Knop Affiliation: Google Amer Sinha Affiliation: Google Lingpeng Kong Affiliation: The University of Hong Kong Ben Kao Affiliation: The University of Hong Kong Ravi Kumar Affiliation: Google Pritish Kamath Corresponding author: qiushisun@connect.hku.hk, pritishk@google.com Affiliation: Google Abstract Building and scaling computer-using agents (CUAs) across desktop, mobile, and web environments requires reliable task-completion verification for data curation, evaluation, and reinforcement learning. Typical automated approaches prompt vision-language models (VLMs) to judge trajectories or generate programs to inspect application state. However, both rely on partial views of complex digital environments. VLM judges are restricted to supplied observations, while generated programs depend on accessible state. These views can omit decisive evidence or leave completion judgments unsupported. Tailoring separate verifiers to different platforms and access settings adds further engineering cost. We present VeriCUA, a platform-agnostic framework for verification through agentic exploration. It treats verification as dynamic evidence gathering and assessment within a shared procedure for online and offline settings across platforms and observation modalities. After inspecting the available context to construct a task rubric, the verifier selects GUI or code checks for unresolved requirements and combines their findings under explicit evidence rules. Experiments show improved agreement with reference labels over the compared baselines across these settings, with the largest offline gains on hard cases and stronger rejection of false completion claims online. Further analyses connect these gains to complementary evidence and test-time exploration. 1 Introduction Vision-language models (VLMs) have enabled computer-using agents (CUAs) to navigate the digital world through software interfaces ( Xie et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ; Rawles et al., 2025 ) . Given a natural-language instruction, an agent observes the interface, plans, and acts, leaving a trajectory of thoughts, actions, and observations. Digital tasks span applications in which success can depend on visual presentation, application records, or changes to persisted files. A trajectory can appear successful even when edits remain unsaved or an operation fails without a visible warning. The agent may also report completion after fulfilling only part of the instruction. Accepting such a run as successful produces a false positive, making the distinction between attempted actions and their actual effects central to verification. Developing these agents therefore requires reliable judgments throughout evaluation, data curation ( Sun et al., 2025 ) , and reinforcement learning ( Xue et al., 2026a ) , including applications for which no task-specific checker has been supplied. An execution can be verified online from the resulting machine state or offline from its retained trajectory. Evidence can come from rendered interfaces, structured observations, or artifacts such as files and database records. VLM judges assess trajectories from selected observations ( Pan et al., 2024 ) , while automatically generated checkers inspect application state through model-written programs ( Xue et al., 2026b ) . A fixed set of frames may omit a decisive effect, and a generated query may target state that does not answer the verification question. Platform-native signals support more specialized judgments and validation ( Chae et al., 2025 ; Sun et al., 2026b ) , but their availability varies with the application and access setting. Agentic approaches actively inspect trajectories or environments ( Wan et al., 2026 ; Cui et al., 2026 ; Sanayei et al., 2026 ) . A shared procedure must seek relevant evidence under these access constraints and ground its conclusions in the observations. Figure 1 : VeriCUA inspects the available environment or recording before constructing a rubric, then gathers evidence to verify its requirements. To address these evidence and access limitations, we present VeriCUA, a platform-agnostic framework that formulates CUA verification as agentic exploration (Figure 1 ). It provides a shared procedure for offline and online verification using the sources and inspection tools available in each setting. Verification begins after the executing agent’s attempt ends. The verifier first explores the available context to understand the app and its task artifacts, then uses these observations with the instruction to construct a rubric of fine-grained requirements. This context helps interpret task concepts and locate potential evidence, especially when the application is unfamiliar. The verifier chooses GUI or code tools to check the rubric’s requirements. Findings from these checks reveal what remains unresolved and guide further inspection of relevant frames, artifacts, or another available source. VeriCUA’s unified design separates the verification workflow from the interfaces through which evidence is obtained. Offline verification navigates retained screen frames and action logs, using structured observations such as accessibility trees when recorded. Online verification can inspect the accessible machine state left by the executing agent through GUI or code tools, including files, databases, and system services. These sources answer different questions about the requested outcome. An action log records an attempted edit, while a file read can show whether the edited content persisted. A report that the task is complete remains a claim to verify. The framework links findings to their supporting observations and records source properties such as frame timing or state persistence. Explicit evidence rules combine the findings into a task verdict while retaining which requirements are supported, refuted, or unresolved. We evaluate this shared procedure in offline and online scenarios on multiple platforms. VeriCUA achieves higher agreement with reference labels than the compared baselines in both settings. It also rejects more false completion claims than the VLM judge in the online study. The action-space study shows that adding code-based state reads enables more decisions without increasing false positives. At a matched number of verification passes, adding visual evidence improves agreement and decision coverage compared with repeating the same configuration. Our contributions are summarized below: • General-Purpose Agentic Verification. VeriCUA formulates CUA verification as agentic exploration, providing a shared paradigm for offline and online tasks across platforms and available evidence sources. • Adaptive Evidence Gathering. Context inspection grounds task rubrics in the available environment or recording. The verifier selects GUI or code checks for unresolved requirements and combines findings under source-specific evidence rules. • Evaluation Across Platforms. Experiments show improved agreement with reference labels across the evaluated platforms. Analyses show how evidence access and complementary exploration affect decision coverage and reliability. 2 Related Work Computer-Using Agents and Their Evaluation. Computer-using agents are evaluated on web, mobile, and desktop tasks ( Zhou et al., 2024 ; Rawles et al., 2025 ; Xie et al., 2024 ) , with dedicated environments covering scientific applications ( Sun et al., 2026c ) . These benchmarks typically use task-specific programmatic evaluators to check the resulting application state. Human-labeled trajectory datasets provide reference judgments across applications ( Sun et al., 2026a ) , while audits of benchmark evaluators identify errors in the checks used to produce reference labels ( Xie et al., 2025 ) . Benchmarks of environment-aware judges assess evidence acquisition and verification of states and execution processes ( Shi et al., 2026 ) . Completion judgments also support data curation and training beyond benchmark evaluation. Trajectory synthesis pipelines use verifier scores to select examples ( Sun et al., 2025 ) , and continual reinforcement learning relies on automated feedback during environment adaptation ( Xue et al., 2026a ) . Rubric-based reward modeling further uses synthetic criteria derived from preferred and rejected responses ( Liu et al., 2026 ) . Safety-oriented evaluation additionally examines whether agent behavior satisfies workflow constraints ( Sun et al., 2026b ) . The range of applications and evaluation criteria creates demand for verification that can locate relevant evidence through available interfaces, including tasks without a dedicated evaluator. Verifying Trajectories and Reward Models. VLM judges assess task completion from trajectory observations ( Pan et al., 2024 ) , while structured critics evaluate task requirements or intermediate milestones ( Li et al., 2026 ) . Task-adaptive rubrics can be generated from task descriptions to guide trajectory evaluation ( Ding, 2026 ) . Generated verifiers construct programs that inspect application state ( Xue et al., 2026b ) . Reward benchmarks evaluate the reliability of trajectory judgments against reference labels across tasks and platforms ( Sun et al., 2026a ; Lin et al., 2025 ) . Agent-based evaluators assess intermediate task requirements in code-generation workflows ( Zhuge et al., 2025 ) . Agentic approaches gather additional evidence by iteratively inspecting recorded trajectories ( Wan et al., 2026 ) or interacting with the execution environment ( Cui et al., 2026 ) . Evidence-first verification separates investigation from validation, checking proposed claims against their state or trace sources before accepting rubric verdicts ( Sanayei et al., 2026 ) . These approaches motivate both seeking task-relevant evidence and assessing how it supports a judgment. VeriCUA builds its rubric after inspecting the available environment or recording, then selects GUI or code checks for unresolved requirements. Source-aware rules combine the resulting findings within a shared offline and online verification workflow. 3 Method 3.1 Verification as Active Evidence Gathering Given an instruction g g , an executing agent produces a trajectory τ = [ o 0 , a 0 , … , o T ] \tau=[o_{0},a_{0},\ldots,o_{T}] of observations and actions, together with any recorded reasoning, and leaves the environment in state s T s_{T} . VeriCUA begins after this attempt ends and assesses whether the execution fulfilled g g using the sources available to the verifier. Although task completion is binary, the verifier outputs y ∈ { success , fail , abstain } y\in\{\textsc{success},\textsc{fail},\textsc{abstain}\} , allowing abstention when the gathered evidence is insufficient to support a decision. The available sources 𝒮 = { S 1 , … , S m } \mathcal{S}=\{S_{1},\ldots,S_{m}\} can include a retained trajectory, recorded accessibility trees ( a11ytrees ), a frozen machine snapshot, or accessible post-execution machine state. Offline verification uses retained observations, while online verification can inspect exposed machine state alongside any retained execution records. When a requirement concerns a change made during execution, an available pre-execution reference can also serve as a source. The shared workflow in Figure 1 begins with context inspection , which gathers information about the application and available observations into context c c . Rubric synthesis uses g g and c c to produce requirements R R that make the instruction checkable. During active exploration , the verifier selects checks for these requirements and uses their results to decide what to inspect next. Finally, rule-based arbitration combines the findings under the setting’s evidence rules and handles any unresolved requirements. At step k k , an inspection action α k = ( v k , x k ) ∈ 𝒜 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \alpha_{k}=(v_{k},x_{k})\in\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}) pairs a tool v k v_{k} with arguments x k x_{k} . Let ℰ k − 1 \mathcal{E}_{k-1} denote the inspection record before this step, initialized with any retained context-inspection outputs ℰ 0 \mathcal{E}_{0} . The verifier selects and executes the next check according to α k ∼ π V ( ⋅ ∣ g , c , R , ℰ k − 1 ) , Execute ( α k , 𝒮 ) ⟶ ( o ~ k , t k ) , \alpha_{k}\sim\pi_{V}(\,\cdot\mid g,c,R,\mathcal{E}_{k-1}),\qquad\operatorname{Execute}(\alpha_{k},\mathcal{S})\longrightarrow(\tilde{o}_{k},t_{k}), (1) where o ~ k \tilde{o}_{k} is the returned tool observation and t k t_{k} records its evidence type and source attributes, assigned by the tool-execution layer (the harness ). The executed check ( α k , o ~ k , t k ) (\alpha_{k},\tilde{o}_{k},t_{k}) and its associated findings are added to form ℰ k \mathcal{E}_{k} . A finding assesses how an observation supports or refutes a particular rubric requirement. The verifier continues until the hard requirements are settled or its inspection budget is exhausted. After L L inspection steps, the arbiter derives a verdict from ℰ L \mathcal{E}_{L} . 3.2 Environment-Aware Rubric Synthesis An instruction specifies the requested result but may leave its application-specific interpretation implicit. A request to save a note, for example, does not necessarily identify the application’s storage directory or explain which view reveals whether the note persisted. Generating requirements without this context can introduce assumptions about files or interface elements that the application does not expose. Before constructing the rubric, VeriCUA uses the available inspection tools to gather context c c . Online inspection can identify application packages, relevant directories, and exposed database schemas; offline inspection reviews the recorded steps, frames, and available structured observations. From the instruction g g and observed context c c , the verifier constructs a rubric R = { ( r i , h i ) } i = 1 n R=\{(r_{i},h_{i})\}_{i=1}^{n} , where each r i r_{i} is a checkable task requirement and h i ∈ { hard , soft } h_{i}\in\{\text{hard},\text{soft}\} indicates whether it is mandatory for success or an additional check. Requirements can concern a resulting state or a change relative to an available pre-execution reference. Each hard requirement must be justified by the outcomes requested in the instruction, while context supplies its application-specific meaning and helps locate evidence. In the note-saving example, the requested text and persistence are task requirements; a discovered directory is a place to inspect for evidence. Each read retains its source attributes. The action space connects the rubric to the sources that can answer its requirements. Figure 2 distinguishes three views of task state: • Trajectory. Retained frames, actions, and reasoning record what the executing agent observed and attempted. The verifier can search the action log, inspect selected frames, and read recorded a11ytrees when available. • Surface. The current machine interface can be inspected through a new screenshot or a UI hierarchy read. A recorded screenshot belongs to the historical trajectory; this view provides a fresh observation of the accessible machine. • Persisted State. Files, application databases, and stored settings can retain effects that the current interface does not show. Code tools can inspect them through file reads, database queries, or queries to exposed services. The harness records persistence for each read. Alongside stored artifacts, live machine access provides volatile observations such as current UI dumps and harness artifacts. GUI tools support visual inspection through frame selection, region enlargement, and optical character recognition (OCR), while code tools query exposed machine state. The online verifier can also synthesize a checker : a sequence of permitted reads paired with a predicate that evaluates a requirement. The harness executes the reads; structured predicates use a restricted evaluator, while visual or semantic comparisons use a model judgment. A single online inspection action α k \alpha_{k} can execute a checker comprising several reads and its predicate evaluation. The verifier chooses its next inspection from the findings already collected, focusing on requirements that remain unresolved within the available access. A text match may leave persistence unresolved and prompt a file read; an unclear frame may prompt a crop or inspection of a later frame. The harness records the executed tool, arguments, and source metadata, including frame timing or the persistence of queried state. The executed read determines these attributes, which are attached to the resulting findings. The complete tool inventory is given in Appendix A.2 . 3.4 Evidence Discipline VeriCUA links each finding to an executed read, then applies source constraints and corroboration rules before assigning requirement statuses. The harness rejects citations that match no executed call and attaches each valid citation’s observation and source attributes to the finding. Source attributes and corroborating probes then determine how each linked assessment contributes to a requirement’s status. Source-Aware Evidence. The attested / asserted source labels distinguish observations of task state from records of the executing agent’s intent or claims. A post-action frame, a file read, or a database query can provide attested evidence. The executing agent’s completion message and a pre-action frame showing an intended operation are asserted evidence for that operation’s outcome. Asserted evidence can direct further inspection but cannot alone mark a requirement met . For example, a screen displaying edited text can support its visible contents, while a file read can check whether that text was saved.
